feedback_note: Reviews caution against framing a single-city activity as an industry-wide trend, while still valuing a balanced mix of community stories. This edition presents Bacolod's tournament only as a specific local example, focusing on its beginner safeguards, charity contribution, free clinic, and player pathway.
feedback_note_zh: 反馈提醒不要把单一城市活动写成行业整体趋势，同时也认可内容中保留社区故事。本期仅将巴科洛德赛事作为一个地方案例，重点介绍新手组别审核、公益捐款、免费体验课和选手晋级机会。

stories.title: Bacolod tournament links 530 players with clinic and charity
stories.title_zh: 巴科洛德赛事汇聚 530 名选手，并安排公益体验课
stories.summary: Bacolod’s first Mayor Greg Gasataya tournament opened Nov. 27 with 530 players in five divisions and a ₱1 million prize pool. Organizers will donate part of entry fees to charity, hold a free clinic, and select a local player for a fully funded Manila competition. The city government lists women’s doubles in several divisions and limits beginner/novice entries to eligible Bacolod residents. This is a local community example, not evidence of a wider trend.
stories.summary_zh: 首届 Mayor Greg Gasataya 匹克球赛于 11 月 27 日在巴科洛德开赛，530 名选手参加五个组别角逐，总奖金为 100 万菲律宾比索。主办方将把部分报名费捐作公益，并计划在赛后举办免费体验课、选出一名当地选手资助其前往马尼拉参赛。市政府公告列出多个女子双打组别，并表示新手和初级组仅面向符合条件的巴科洛德居民。这只是一个地方社区案例，不能据此推断整个行业趋势。
stories.why: The event shows concrete ways a local tournament can welcome new players: resident-focused beginner divisions, a free clinic, and a next-step competition opportunity.
stories.why_zh: 这场赛事展示了地方比赛吸引新手的具体做法：面向居民的新手组、免费体验课，以及后续参赛机会。
stories.source: Digicast Negros; Bacolod City Communications Office
